Traditional Mince Pies

Served at: Fourth Sunday of Advent

Makes 12 piesPrep 30 min (plus 30 min chilling)Cook 15-20 min

Mince Pies are a quintessential British Christmas treat, traditionally enjoyed throughout the Advent season and especially on Christmas Day. These delightful small pies, filled with a rich, spiced fruit mixture, are a symbol of festive cheer and a delicious way to count down to the holiday, perfect for the Fourth Sunday of Advent.

Ingredients

  • 225 grams (1 3/4 cups) all-purpose flour, plus extra for dusting
  • 110 grams (1/2 cup) cold unsalted butter, cubed
  • 50 grams (1/4 cup) caster sugar (superfine sugar)
  • 1 large egg yolk
  • 2-3 tablespoons ice cold water
  • Approximately 400 grams (14 ounces) good quality jarred mincemeat
  • 1 large egg, beaten (for egg wash)
  • 1 tablespoon caster sugar, for sprinkling

Method

  1. In a large bowl, rub the cold butter into the flour with your fingertips until the mixture resembles fine breadcrumbs. Alternatively, pulse in a food processor.
  2. Stir in the caster sugar.
  3. Add the egg yolk and 2 tablespoons of ice cold water. Mix with a knife or your hands until the dough just comes together. If it's too dry, add the remaining tablespoon of water, a little at a time.
  4. Gently bring the dough together into a ball, flatten slightly into a disc, wrap in plastic wrap, and chill in the refrigerator for at least 30 minutes.
  5. Preheat your oven to 200°C (400°F). Lightly grease a 12-hole muffin tin.
  6. On a lightly floured surface, roll out about two-thirds of the chilled pastry to a thickness of about 3mm (1/8 inch).
  7. Using a 7.5 cm (3-inch) round cutter, cut out 12 circles for the pie bases. Carefully press each circle into the prepared muffin tin holes.
  8. Spoon about 1-2 tablespoons of mincemeat into each pastry case, filling them almost to the top.
  9. Roll out the remaining pastry. Using a 6 cm (2.5-inch) round cutter or a star-shaped cutter, cut out 12 lids or decorative tops.
  10. Place a lid on top of each pie. If using round lids, gently press the edges to seal. If using star shapes, simply place them on top of the mincemeat.
  11. Brush the tops of the pies with the beaten egg wash and sprinkle lightly with caster sugar.
  12. Bake for 15-20 minutes, or until the pastry is golden brown and the filling is bubbling slightly.
  13. Let the mince pies cool in the tin for 5-10 minutes before carefully transferring them to a wire rack to cool completely. Serve warm or at room temperature.

Tips

  • For extra flavor, you can add a teaspoon of brandy or orange zest to the mincemeat before filling the pies.
  • Mince pies freeze beautifully. Bake and cool them completely, then freeze in an airtight container for up to 3 months. Reheat in a moderate oven until warmed through.
  • If you prefer a richer pastry, you can use half butter and half lard for a flakier texture.
